description:
Found by the fz-kdt.104 cold review's prototype (2026-08-31): with canonical clause order in place, FIFO+sort vs LIFO+sort on enum_predicate_search still differ 221 vs 207 executables -- 14 FIFO-only specializations on over-wide inputs (int | :false | :ok | :true). Stdout identical; the class is schedule-dependent DEMAND of transient wide joins (a spec minted for an intermediate join that a different schedule never materializes). Covered by neither fz-kdt.101 (display) nor fz-kdt.104/105 (dispatch/keys). Diagnose after 104+105 land: is this the fz-kdt.63-noted return-widening ladder shape, or demand issued from mid-ascent evidence that later narrows? Instrument: spec-set diff under the LIFO recipe at the post-105 base.

## BLOCKED BY

- ○ fz-kdt.104 P1 Dispatch arm order is semantics when a narrow arm is runtime-indistinguishable from its wide sibling: drop runtime-shadowed arms (P1 miscompile)

DISPUTED REPORT, RE-VERIFY BEFORE DIAGNOSING (2026-08-31): the fz-kdt.104
refuter reported a harness-vs-production lens divergence at the kdt.104
landing (predicate 217 harness vs 182 production; 00277 UP 180->185 with
truly-new Kernel.dbg keys), claimed run-to-run stable. The kdt.104
builder then COULD NOT REPRODUCE it: all three production doors (run /
interp / build --dump backend=) x5 runs each, both sides of the change,
agree md5-stable at 217/180 -- and it identified two concrete measurement
traps the refuter may have hit (a --dump <path>.canon path selects a
DIFFERENT dump kind with no executable lines; fixture 00421 has no main/0
and produces no dump, so comparing its "dump" compares garbage). Status:
the divergence is UNPROVEN; treat it as a measurement-methodology caution
until someone reproduces it with explicit dump-kind syntax and md5s. The
rest of this paragraph preserves the original claim for reference:
ORIGINAL CLAIM (unreproduced):  the class also surfaces as a
HARNESS-vs-PRODUCTION LENS DIVERGENCE introduced by fz-kdt.104's
otherwise-sound arm filter: at its base both lenses agreed on
enum_predicate_search (221/221); after the filter the canon_test harness
lens (drive_root_to_dump_stage) reads 217 while the production front
doors (fz2 run / fz2 interp --dump backend=) read 182 -- a 36-executable
production-only shrink -- and 00277_enum_tier0_fixture moves UPWARD on
the production lens only (180->185: truly-new Kernel.dbg/1[empty_list()]
+ Kernel.fz_dbg_value/1[empty_list()], four keys doubling, one
Range.reduce/5 gone). Behavior byte-identical throughout, so the
divergence is spec-set-only -- but it means THE TWO LENSES RUN DIFFERENT
SCHEDULES and the demand of transient joins depends on it, which is this
ticket's disease in a second costume. Diagnose both together: the 14
FIFO-only over-wide specs AND the lens divergence should fall to one
explanation (demand issued from mid-ascent evidence that a different
schedule never materializes). Repro: dump both lenses at the fz-kdt.104
landing and diff key sets.

comments.text: fz-kdt.105 measurement (post-landing, door = fz2 interp --dump backend=, release build): the FIFO-vs-LIFO key-set gap on enum_predicate_search falls from 35 keys to exactly 14. Base fba7d72e3: FIFO 217 keys, LIFO 182, 35 FIFO-only. With canonical clause order: FIFO 217, LIFO 203, 14 FIFO-only, zero LIFO-only. Every one of the surviving 14 carries the same over-wide join 'int | :false | :ok | :true' (Enum.all?/1#lambda@4125-4170/2, three Enum.all?/2#lambda@4286-4337/2, Enum.all_value_step/1, Enum.empty?/1#lambda@4753-4792/2, Kernel.</2, Kernel.==/2, Kernel.fz_op_eq/2, Kernel.fz_op_lt/2 and siblings) -- i.e. the 21 that vanished were the clause-ORDER class and the 14 that remain are exactly this ticket's transient-wide-join class, now isolated with nothing else mixed in. 00420 and 00183 are fully key-confluent FIFO vs LIFO at both base and head.

title: 14 FIFO-only over-wide specializations on enum_predicate_search: schedule-dependent demand of transient wide joins
